subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should credential-shaped keys explicitly configured in `skills.entries.<skill>.env` bypass the generic sensitive-name block for that active skill's host run while dangerous host override names remain blocked?
rationale: The source and docs support the regression, but the repair intentionally changes which credentials can reach executable children and must be reconciled with the open inverse secret-leak issue.

options.title: Allow configured skill env secrets with isolation
options.body: Permit credential-shaped keys explicitly present in the active skill config, add tests for gog-like delivery and dangerous-name rejection, and strip unrelated active skill secrets from generic exec children.

options.title: Keep metadata-only sensitive allowlist
options.body: Require skills to declare every sensitive env name through metadata and update docs or doctor guidance so configured-only credential-shaped env keys are not expected to work.

options.title: Defer to a broader credential contract
options.body: Pause this bypass until maintainers define a broader SecretRef or plugin-owned credential path for CLI skills that need headless auth.

recommendation.title: Allow configured skill env secrets with isolation
recommendation.body: Permit credential-shaped keys explicitly present in the active skill config, add tests for gog-like delivery and dangerous-name rejection, and strip unrelated active skill secrets from generic exec children.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has recent merged history on overlapping skill env and SecretRef runtime behavior and is the strongest current routing candidate for the decision.
